title: A Team Workflow for Focused Changes
description: Explore standard industry branching workflows, master built-in help commands, apply core best practices, and review essential Git vocabulary.

blocks.content: A **workflow** is the agreed-upon process your team follows for how changes move from an idea to the main codebase. Without a workflow, people step on each other's work. The most common pattern for teams is the **feature branch workflow**.

## The Feature Branch Workflow

The idea is simple: all new work goes on its own branch. Main (or master) is always in a working state.

```
1. git switch main
2. git pull                        # start from the latest code
3. git switch -c feature/my-thing  # create your branch
   ... make changes ...
4. git add .                       # stage
5. git commit -m "add my thing"    # commit
6. git push origin feature/my-thing # push branch to remote
7. Open a pull request for review
8. After approval, merge into main
9. git switch main && git pull     # update your local main
10. git branch -d feature/my-thing # clean up
```

## Writing Good Commit Messages

A good message explains **what and why**, not how:

```
# Good
add password reset email with 24-hour expiry link
fix cart total not updating after quantity change

# Bad
fix
wip
changes
```

## Key Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **repository (repo)** | A project folder tracked by Git, including all its history |
| **commit** | A saved snapshot of staged changes |
| **branch** | An independent line of development |
| **merge** | Combining two branches into one |
| **remote** | A copy of the repository stored on a server |
| **origin** | The default name Git gives to the remote you cloned from |
| **HEAD** | A pointer to your current position in the repository |
| **staging area** | The collection of changes ready for the next commit |

blocks.question: In the feature branch workflow, what is the purpose of keeping `main` always in a working state?
options: So Git doesn't run out of storage
So the team always has a stable version to deploy or branch from
Because Git prevents commits directly to main
So pull requests are automatically approved
blocks.explanation: The whole point of the feature branch workflow is that `main` is always deployable. New work goes on feature branches, gets reviewed via pull requests, and only merges into `main` when it's ready. This means the team always has a known-good version to work from.
